page: Amazon Web Services x8aedz.metal-12xl is a bare-metal memory-optimized server powered by 48 dedicated physical cores of the AMD EPYC 9R05 processor on the x86_64 architecture. Operating at up to 5.0 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, it delivers one execution thread per core alongside 1536 GB of system RAM, allocating an extensive 32 GB of memory per core. The server includes 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and provides a baseline network throughput of 38 Gbps, with zero GPUs provisioned.

Benchmark results place the platform in the top tier across synthetic and memory-intensive evaluations. The dedicated 48-core topology achieved a stress-ng multi-core score of 201580.87 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 33092.0. Memory subsystems exhibited uncached read bandwidth of 536.36 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 214.24 GB/sec on large 256 MB block transfers, supporting a PassMark database score of 41873.32 and 176.61 million Redis SET operations per second.

By eliminating hypervisor virtualization overhead, the bare-metal design guarantees consistent memory bandwidth and predictable single-thread execution latency. The hardware profile provides high memory density per compute core alongside rapid NVMe scratch space, though workloads demanding GPU acceleration must look elsewhere. These attributes make the platform suited for large-scale in-memory caching systems, high-concurrency relational databases, real-time analytics engines, and CPU-driven language model inference.
description: Amazon Web Services x8aedz.metal-12xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance engineered for large-scale data systems. Driven by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R05 processor with 48 dedicated physical cores clocking at 5.0 GHz and 1 thread per core, the server pairs compute power with 1536 GB of system memory, yielding 32 GB per core. Local storage is provided by a 3800 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a 38 Gbps baseline network interface, while discrete GPUs are absent. The platform demonstrates top-tier benchmark outcomes, reaching 536.36 GB/sec in uncached read memory bandwidth and over 176 million Redis SET operations per second. Hypervisor-free execution ensures maximum resource isolation and sustained throughput without multithreading jitter. This bare-metal architecture delivers favorable resource density for memory-intensive enterprise tasks, making it suited for in-memory key-value databases, large relational database hosting, extensive data analytics pipelines, and CPU-based LLM inference workloads.
